blocks.text: • Each participant is responsible for action and inaction within their role.
• Starting works without an approved project, cost estimate or contract is prohibited.
• Absence of a contract or HSE documents for a worker is the responsibility of the PM and the HSE Engineer.
• Failure to comply with the requirements of this Regulation is grounds for disciplinary action.
• Absence of documentary confirmation of work completion is equated to non-completion.
• Any verbal agreements must be recorded in writing.

items: Payments to contractors and wages - only after Technical Supervision signs the certificates. In plain words: until Technical Supervision signs the certificate, nobody gets paid. No exceptions and no "we'll submit the rest later."
Every payment - only from the payment register, with the "contract" column filled in and the initiator visible. A payment without a contract is not processed in the register.
Monthly payment - only after the PTD technical verification note (see "Monthly cycle"). PTD is a filter: it catches overruns and unexplained works BEFORE money goes out.
Verbal agreements do not exist. If it was said, record it in Worksection or in the minutes. If it is not recorded, the agreement does not exist and cannot be referenced.
Every meeting ends with minutes: date, attendees, decisions made, assignee, due date. A decision not entered into the decision register is considered not made.

Any change to the project, cost estimate or schedule - only in writing, via a Change Request (App. Г1). "Let's just do it a bit differently here" without paperwork is unauthorized work that is not paid for.
Every document has a status and a version. We work only with the current version; using an outdated version is the mistake of whoever picked it up.
Design documentation reaches the site only through PTD, stamped "Issued for Construction." Drawings "from the architect's phone" are not a document.
A contract - with everyone: contractor, crew, even a single individual. No contract - the person does not work on site.
Any procurement - a minimum of 3 commercial offers and a comparison table: price / lead time / warranty / who was chosen and why (App. В7).

Tenders are organized by the Client's Service, with the Project Manager participating. Material supply goes through the Procurement Dept as an internal contractor, not "someone we know will bring it."
Prices for materials and works are controlled by PTD together with the Cost Engineer - continuously, not only when something "seems expensive."
Machinery is ordered for the site tied to the Works Schedule (App. В2, В3). Responsible - Site Manager and mechanic. Idle machinery is money burning every day.
Fuel consumption norms are approved; tracking is instrument-based (engine hours, fuel sensors, GPS), cash use is minimal. A Machinery Timesheet is kept for every unit - every shift.
Inventory items and fixed assets are tracked and inventoried through project completion. Everything handed over goes through a transfer certificate of responsibility (App. В6).
A daily site summary instead of a daily meeting: headcount by 8:30, photos throughout the day, progress and issues - in the Telegram chat with Head of CS.
Photo documentation - per checklist (App. Д4): general view, concealed works, reinforcement, engineering systems, details, dated. Mandatory before closing a Concealed Works Acceptance Certificate.
The monthly cycle is the law: plan by the 25th, reporting package by the 5th, PTD verification note by the 10th (see "Monthly cycle").
Reports are generated from system exports for the period, not rewritten by hand - less manual work, fewer errors.
A request left unanswered within the standard term is escalated automatically (see "Overdue escalation") - no need to "remind anyone personally."
A project without a complete startup package is not passed into execution (see "Startup package"). Started without the package - the works are unauthorized.

A Concealed Works Acceptance Certificate may be issued for a structure as a whole or for part of it within specific axes.

blocks.text: The Client's Service and Technical Supervision have the right to stop works in the event of:

items: safety violations;
deviation from the design;
missing documentation;
poor quality of works;
use of unapproved materials.

blocks.text: Procedure for stopping and resuming works

items: The initiator (Technical Supervision / HSE engineer / Head of CS) draws up a stoppage certificate: grounds, scope of stopped works, requirements for remediation.
The certificate is submitted the same day to the PM, Site Manager and Head of CS; the Head of CS notifies the CEO.
The contractor remedies the violations and notifies in writing of readiness for inspection.
Resumption of works - only with the initiator's written permission, approved by the Head of CS.
Downtime caused by the contractor is not compensated; losses are recorded in the claims register.

blocks.text: PTD is the single point for issuing documentation. A document obtained bypassing PTD is considered unregistered and is not grounds for works or payments.
The rule is simple: every touchpoint with another department has a specific form, a specific deadline, and a specific answer. Below are typical situations.
Procurement Dept (supply) - our internal contractor for materials

items: Materials needed → Site Foreman / Site Manager submits a request (App. В1) tied to the monthly plan → response within 2 business days → delivery by the deadline stated in the request.
Together with the monthly plan (by the 25th), the site submits a consolidated materials requirement with delivery deadlines - Procurement orders in advance, not "yesterday".
Every delivery arrives with quality documents (certificates, data sheets). Without documents, material is not accepted into works under acceptance certificates.

blocks.text: Financial Dept - money moves only against confirmed documents

items: We provide: acts signed by Technical Supervision, payment register, funding schedule, PTD Technical Verification Note. Without this package, Financial Dept does not process the payment.
They provide: payments within 3 business days after initiation with the complete package, a monthly budget execution report, project limits.
The question "where is my payment?" - request via Head of CS, response within 2 business days (see "Request Routes" section).

We receive the concept and initial data at the initiation and design stages; we return feedback on feasibility and cost before the cost estimate is approved.

blocks.text: Rule: a report not submitted on time is considered not submitted. From there, escalation applies (section "Overdue Escalation") along with the sanctions in Appendix А.

This is the main rhythm of site work. It's simple: record the facts daily, reconcile the schedule weekly, plan next month by the 25th, submit last month by the 5th, PTD checks it by the 10th, then payment follows. Skip a step and the money stops.

items: By 8:30 - the Site Manager posts in the Telegram chat with the Head of CS: how many people showed up on site (by crew).
During the day - 3-5 photos of key zones in the same chat, showing what is actually being done.
The Site Foreman fills in the work performance log. The driver / mechanic fills in the timesheet for each piece of equipment (App. В5).

By 17:00 - schedule plan-vs-actual: if everything is on schedule, the schedule is submitted marked as compliant. If there is a delay, the Site Manager explains the reasons to the PM in writing (free form) and what is being done to catch up.
By 17:00 - weekly photo report per procedure (App. Е5): every job of the week is on a photo that clearly shows WHAT was done.
By 18:00 - the week's equipment timesheets go to PTD (signed by the Site Manager).
Along with the timesheets - delivery notes and certificates for materials received during the week.

By the 25th - the Site Manager submits to PTD the work plan for the next month (App. Б1) + schedule (App. Б2) + material requirements with delivery dates. No plan means the next month is not funded and materials are not ordered.
By the 28th - PTD reconciles the plan against the design, cost estimate and cumulative works register, and forwards the material requirements to Procurement.

By the 5th of the following month - the Site Manager submits the reporting package for the past month (App. Б3): work completion certificate signed by the Site Manager and Technical Supervision + equipment timesheets + as-built documentation (concealed works acceptance certificates, certificates, drawings) + delivery notes. If one document is missing, the package is not accepted.

By the 10th - PTD checks the package, reconciles it with the cumulative works register, and sends the technical verification note to the Head of Client's Service. This is a filter: if PTD finds overruns or unexplained work, the package is sent back for revision.
After the technical verification note - the Head of Client's Service approves the certificates, and Finance processes payment (within the limits set out in the "Authority Matrix" section).

blocks.text: PTD technical verification note - payment filter

items: The technical verification note is PTD's final monthly reconciliation: completed works against the plan and cost estimate, materials written off against norms, equipment operation against timesheets.

PTD checks the site's full reporting package (work completion certificate + equipment timesheets + as-built documentation + delivery notes and certificates) and submits the technical verification note to the Head of Client's Service by the 10th.
Certificates go to the Head of Client's Service for approval only after PTD review. The month's payment is not confirmed without the technical verification note.
Any unforeseen work (dismantling, rework, reinforcement) is carried out only through a Change Request (App. Г1) issued before the work begins.
Chain: the Site Foreman records the issue → the Site Manager initiates the change → the Head of Client's Service approves it. The schedule is adjusted at the same time, with the reason stated.
Work performed without a registered change is considered unauthorized and is not paid for.
The impact on budget and schedule is recorded in the change form and in the budget variance register.
